name: MT25QU128ABA1EW7-0SIT
title: 128 Mb 1.8 V serial NOR flash with dual and quad I/O, STR and DTR
summary: MT25QU128ABA is a 128 Mbit (16 MB) serial NOR flash running from 1.7 V to 2.0 V, with an SPI-compatible bus that also moves address and data on two or four lines, at single or double transfer rate (166 MHz STR, 90 MHz DTR). It erases in 4KB, 32KB and 64KB blocks or as a whole, programs 256-byte pages, and adds execute-in-place, program/erase suspend, per-sector volatile and nonvolatile locks with optional password, a 64-byte OTP area and an on-chip CRC-64 check. MT25QU128ABA1EW7-0SIT is the HOLD# version in the 6 x 5 mm W-PDFN-8, standard grade, -40 °C to +85 °C.

pins.name: S#
pins.function: Chip select, active low. High deselects the part (standby once any internal cycle ends), floats the outputs and ignores the other inputs. A falling edge is needed after power-up before the first command.

pins.name: DQ1
pins.function: Serial data 1. Data output for x1 commands; bidirectional in dual and quad transfers.

pins.name: W#/DQ2
pins.function: Write protect input, and DQ2 in quad transfers. With status register bit 7 at 1, holding it low makes the nonvolatile status bits read-only. No internal pull-up: it must be driven even when unused.

pins.name: VSS
pins.function: Ground for the core and the I/O.

pins.name: DQ0
pins.function: Serial data 0. Data input for x1 commands; bidirectional in dual and quad transfers.

pins.name: C
pins.function: Serial clock. Commands latch on the rising edge. In STR, address and data in latch on the rising edge and data out changes on the falling edge; in DTR both edges carry data in and out.

pins.name: DQ3/HOLD#
pins.function: DQ3 in quad transfers, otherwise HOLD#: low pauses the serial transfer without deselecting; outputs float and inputs are ignored. HOLD# is off in QIO-SPI, in DTR, or when configuration bit 4 is 0. Drive high or pull up when only x1 and x2 commands are used.

pins.name: VCC
pins.function: Supply for the core and the I/O, 1.7 V to 2.0 V.

operation.text: 128 Mbit as 256 sectors of 64KB, each split into 32KB and 4KB subsectors (512 and 4096 of them). Programming goes through a 256-byte buffer, one page at a time; the smallest erase is a 4KB subsector, never a page. A separate 64-byte OTP area sits outside the main array.

Three bus protocols, each in STR or DTR: extended-SPI (x1 commands on DQ0 in, DQ1 out, plus dual and quad commands that use DQ[1:0] or DQ[3:0] for address and data), dual-SPI (everything on DQ[1:0]) and quad-SPI (everything on DQ[3:0]). The protocol comes from the nonvolatile or enhanced volatile configuration register, or from ENTER/RESET QUAD INPUT/OUTPUT MODE, whose effect is immediate and which must not follow WRITE ENABLE. The DTR read commands run in DTR whatever the registers say; all other commands run in DTR only once DTR is set in a register.

Up to 166 MHz in STR and 90 MHz in DTR for every command but READ (03h), which is limited to 54 MHz STR and 27 MHz DTR. The highest usable frequency of each FAST READ depends on the dummy clock count programmed (clock frequency tables). Throughput reaches 90 MB/s with quad I/O.

Every command starts with S# going low and the 8-bit code on DQn. Reads end whenever S# goes high during data out. Writes, programs and erases must end with S# going high on a byte boundary (after the 8th bit of the last byte; the 16th for the nonvolatile configuration register); otherwise they are dropped, no error flag is set and the write enable latch keeps its state. Between RESET ENABLE and RESET MEMORY S# must stay high for tSHSL2.

Address is 3 bytes, A[23:0], sampled on rising clock edges. Data runs from the given address and the address increments after each byte, so one command can read the whole die; past the top it starts again from address 0. FAST READ commands insert dummy clocks after the address and run faster than READ. QUAD INPUT/OUTPUT WORD READ (E7h) needs A0 = 0 and only four dummy clocks; it works in extended- and quad-SPI, not in DTR, and dual-SPI ignores it. The ID commands (9Eh/9Fh, AFh) return manufacturer, device and unique ID bytes; if a program or erase is under way the ID command is not decoded and the cycle carries on.

READ SERIAL FLASH DISCOVERY PARAMETER (5Ah) returns JEDEC JESD216 tables (revision 1.6 content from 2014 week 42 production) from a 3-byte address after 8 dummy clocks. The output wraps to 0 at the 2048-byte boundary and ignores the wrap setting. Contents are in Micron TN-25-06.

WRITE ENABLE (06h) sets the write enable latch; no PROGRAM, ERASE or register WRITE runs without it. WRITE DISABLE (04h) clears it, except after a protection error, which needs CLEAR FLAG STATUS REGISTER to clear both. The latch is cleared at the end of every program, erase or nonvolatile write, pass or fail.

An internal configuration register sets the behaviour. The nonvolatile configuration register is copied into it at power-on and reset; the volatile and enhanced volatile configuration registers overwrite it as soon as their WRITE command ends. Status register writes (tW) and nonvolatile configuration writes (tWNVCR) are self-timed and set write in progress. The nonvolatile configuration register is sent and read least significant byte first; reading it past 16 bits gives 0. The volatile registers return the same byte over and over when read continuously. Status and flag status registers can be read at any time, even during a program or erase.

Programming only turns 1s into 0s. Up to 256 bytes go into one page; a start address not on a page boundary wraps the excess back to the start of the same page, and beyond 256 bytes only the last 256 sent are guaranteed. Bytes not sent keep their old contents. A program to a protected sector is refused: the latch stays set and flag status bits 1 and 4 are set. A timed-out operation clears the latch and sets the program fail bit.

Erasing turns bits back to 1 (FFh). 4KB (20h) and 32KB (52h) subsector, 64KB sector (D8h) and bulk (C7h/60h) erases are self-timed (tSSE, tSE, tBE). Without WRITE ENABLE the erase is ignored and no error bit is set. An erase of a protected area is refused with flag status bits 1 and 5 set; bulk erase is refused if any sector is locked. Any address inside the subsector or sector selects it.

During a program, erase or nonvolatile write, status bit 0 reads 1 and flag status bit 7 reads 0; the operation is over when flag status bit 7 reads 1. Several operations (reset, suspend, OTP program) count as finished only once flag status bit 7 has returned 1 with at least one byte clocked out.

PROGRAM/ERASE SUSPEND (75h) pauses an array program or erase within the suspend latency, setting flag status bit 2 (program) or 6 (erase) and then bit 7. While suspended, reads are allowed anywhere but the suspended page or sector (which returns indeterminate data), and during an erase suspend other sectors can be programmed; a program aimed at the suspended sector is ignored with flag status bit 4 set. If the remaining time is shorter than the latency, the operation simply completes. One level of nesting is allowed: suspend an erase, program elsewhere and suspend that, then two RESUME (7Ah) commands restart the program and then the erase. Suspend state is lost at power-off; the flag status register then powers up as 80h. A resumed erase does not re-check volatile lock bits written meanwhile.

Status bits BP[3:0] and TB protect a power-of-two block of sectors counted from the top or from the bottom of the array, up to all of it. With status bit 7 at 1 and W# low, the nonvolatile status bits are read-only and WRITE STATUS REGISTER does nothing; raising W# is the only way out. tWHSL and tSHWL apply to W# around that write.

Each 64KB sector has a nonvolatile lock bit (locked at 0, erased together back to 1) and a volatile lock bit (locked at 1, cleared by reset or power-down); the first and last sectors take volatile locks per 4KB subsector. A volatile global freeze bit freezes all nonvolatile lock bits. Sector protection register bit 2 or bit 1, one-time programmable, selects password mode or no password for good. In password mode the freeze bit comes up set at every power-up or reset and only UNLOCK PASSWORD with the 64-bit password releases it.

64 bytes plus a control byte (byte 64). READ OTP ARRAY (4Bh) reads from a 3-byte address after dummy clocks; there is no rollover, and reading past 0x40 keeps returning location 0x40. PROGRAM OTP ARRAY (42h), after WRITE ENABLE, takes at most 65 bytes and discards the rest; it runs for tPOTP. Programming bit 0 of the control byte to 0 locks the array permanently.

ENTER DEEP POWER-DOWN (B9h) cuts supply current to ICC2 tDP after S# goes high; it is refused during a write and can serve as software protection. In deep power-down only RELEASE FROM DEEP POWER-DOWN (ABh), RESET ENABLE/RESET MEMORY, hardware reset and the power-loss rescue sequence are accepted; no error bits are set and the write enable latch is unchanged. After ABh the part is in standby tRDP after S# rises, and S# must stay high meanwhile; extra clocks while S# is low cancel ABh. Power-off or a reset also ends deep power-down.

RESET ENABLE (66h) then RESET MEMORY (99h), separated by at least tSHSL2 of S# high, put the part through a power-on reset; it can be selected again after tSHSL3. Volatile lock bits and the volatile and enhanced volatile configuration registers return to the defaults set by the nonvolatile configuration register. A program, erase or write under way or suspended is aborted and its data may be corrupt. RESET ENABLE is refused while a status register write (01h) or a nonvolatile configuration write (B1h) is running; leaving XIP first is advised.

Pin option 1 puts HOLD# on DQ3, option 3 puts RESET# on DQ3, and option 8 (not in 8-pin packages) adds a dedicated RESET# pin with HOLD# on DQ3. Both functions can be turned off with configuration bit 4, and the DQ3 versions are off in quad protocol (HOLD# also in DTR). A RESET# low pulse of at least tRLRH = 50 ns resets the part; recovery time tRHSL depends on what was running. When DQ3 doubles as HOLD# or RESET# and only x1 or x2 commands are used, DQ3 must be driven high or pulled up so that the input never floats.

Execute-in-place drops the command code: after S# toggles, each read needs only an address. To enter from SPI, set volatile configuration bit 3 to 0 and send a FAST READ with the XIP confirmation bit (DQ0 in the first dummy clock) at 0. To boot straight into XIP, program nonvolatile configuration bits 11:9. Sending the confirmation bit as 1 leaves XIP, and the volatile bit 3 returns to 1 by itself. If the host is reset alone, it can leave XIP with DQ0 = 1 for 7, 9, 13, 17, 25 and 33 clocks, each burst with S# raised before the next clock; this does not reset the part or stop a program or erase, so RESET ENABLE and RESET MEMORY follow.

S# must follow VCC (deselected) on the way up until VCC,min and on the way down to VSS. Below the power-on reset threshold the logic is held in reset and ignores every command. During power-up only the two status reads (05h, 70h) are answered, in extended-SPI STR; the part is fully usable tVSL (300 µs max) after VCC,min, and with a fast VCC ramp polling needs at least 100 µs after VWI. During tVSL HOLD# is on, RESET# off and drive strength at default. After power-up the part is in standby with the write enable and write in progress bits clear and both volatile lock bits at 0. Losing power during a write, program or erase may corrupt data.
Decouple VCC at every device with a capacitor near the package pins, typically 100 nF.

operation.topic: Power loss recovery and interface rescue
operation.text: If power fails during WRITE NONVOLATILE CONFIGURATION REGISTER, the part may start in XIP or in an unwanted protocol. Both rescue sequences start with DQ0 and DQ3 at 1 for bursts of 7, 9, 13, 17, 25 and 33 clocks, raising S# before the next clock each time. Power loss recovery then sends DQ0 = DQ3 = 1 for 8 clocks (S# high before the 9th) and leaves the part in extended-SPI, XIP off, until power is cycled. Interface rescue sends 16 such clocks (both edges in DTR, S# high before the 17th); it resets only the interface to the last nonvolatile settings and does not stop operations under way. tSHSL2 must be at least 50 ns throughout; afterwards rewrite the nonvolatile configuration register.

operation.topic: Active, standby and deep power-down modes
operation.text: S# low selects the part (active). With S# high it stays active until internal operations end, then drops to standby (ICC1). Deep power-down (ICC2) is the lowest-current state.

INTERFACE ACTIVATION 9Bh with sub-command 27h computes a CRC-64 over the whole device or an address range and compares it with the expected value sent in the sequence; flag status bit 4 shows the result. On a mismatch the computed CRC is left in the 64-byte volatile general purpose read register (read with 96h, least significant byte first); on a match it reads all 0. That register is zeroed at power-up and reset. Typical check time is 1.3 ms per main block and 0.5 s for the whole 128Mb.
Shipped erased (every byte FFh), status register 00h, nonvolatile configuration register FFFFh, all sectors unlocked.
JESD47H compliant: at least 100,000 erase cycles per sector and 20 years typical data retention.
The W-PDFN exposed pad is pulled to VSS inside the part. Leave it open or connect it to VSS, and to nothing else.
